title: Unverified claim of a 2025 Gina Haspel leak investigation
description_short: The supplied record alleges a 2025 leak investigation targeting Gina Haspel; the packet does not verify that one was opened.
description_medium: The frozen record alleges that the Trump administration opened a classified-leak investigation of former CIA Director Gina Haspel in March 2025, framing it as retaliation. The packet provides no supporting source or case details. A July 2025 Federalist article discusses a proposal to investigate Haspel over Russia-related issues, but does not report the alleged March leak probe. This remains an internal, unverified allegation.
description_long: The frozen record alleges that the Trump administration opened a classified-leak investigation of former CIA Director Gina Haspel on March 20, 2025, over leaks said to have damaged President Trump. It frames the alleged inquiry as retaliation and says critics linked it to Haspel’s earlier handling of intelligence assessments and the Ukraine whistleblower matter. None of those asserted connections is established by the supplied packet: it identifies no agency announcement, case number, charge, named source, or contemporaneous report confirming that a leak investigation was opened. A July 28, 2025 Federalist article reports that Peter Schweizer raised questions about Haspel and argues in its headline that she should be investigated over Russia-related matters. That later commentary does not document a March leak inquiry, and its topic is distinct from the record’s alleged classified-leak probe. This draft preserves the supplied claim as an allegation for internal review. Its date and all attributed conduct remain unverified; do not present them as findings, charges, or proof of retaliation. Before publication, establish whether an official or credible report identifies a specific investigation and supports the claimed subject and date.

title: Unverified allegation of Marshals surveillance targeting federal judges
description_short: The supplied record alleges Marshals surveillance and intimidation of judges; its cited reporting documents judicial-security concerns, not the alleged program.
description_medium: The frozen record alleges that, in March 2025, the Trump administration directed U.S. Marshals to gather intelligence on judges who ruled against it and that armed Marshals appeared at judges’ homes. Its Reuters link instead reports a federal judiciary task force on security and independence amid criticism of judges. It does not report Marshals surveillance or intimidation visits. The allegation remains unverified in this internal draft.
description_long: The frozen record alleges that the Trump administration directed the U.S. Marshals Service in March 2025 to surveil judges whose rulings blocked administration actions, and that armed Marshals appeared at some judges’ homes in a manner witnesses found intimidating. It further says Senate Judiciary members demanded an inquiry and judges filed internal complaints. The input supplies no names, filings, testimony, or source for these claims, so none is established here. The linked Reuters article, published March 26, reports that the federal judiciary launched a task force on security and independence amid Trump and allies’ criticism of judges. It does not report Marshals surveillance or intimidation visits. That account establishes a contemporaneous judicial-security debate, not the alleged program. Protection work by the Marshals and an alleged use of that service for political intelligence are different propositions and require separate evidence. Keep the March 1 start date only as supplied and unverified. This internal draft preserves the allegation for review; it is not a finding or publication-ready account. Before publication, obtain credible evidence identifying the alleged direction, specific incidents, dates, and witnesses, or remove the unsupported details.
date_start_basis: Supplied original date; the specific alleged incidents are unverified.
